subject: feat(ssh_dotnet): wire private-key authentication (key-first, passphrase, clear errors)
body:
feat(ssh_dotnet): wire private-key authentication (key-first, passphrase, clear errors)

Replace the null-returning placeholder: GetAuthenticationMethods now reads
SshDotNetPrivateKeyFile + SshDotNetPrivateKeyPassphrase off the connection and builds
a PrivateKeyAuthenticationMethod via the existing CreatePrivateKeyAuth loader (handles
both passphrase-protected and unprotected keys). Key auth is tried FIRST (OpenSSH
behaviour), then password, then keyboard-interactive. The unused-param + // TODO smells
are gone.

Key-load failures (missing file, wrong passphrase, corrupt key) propagate and are
caught in Connect's TryBuildAuthentication (now catching ArgumentException /
FileNotFoundException / SshException) so the user gets an actionable message instead of
a silent fallback.

UI: the properties already render for SSH_DotNet connections (AttributeUsedInProtocol)
with the passphrase masked (PasswordPropertyText) and localized labels.

Test: GetAuthenticationMethods_ReadsKeyFile_AndSurfacesMissingFile proves the key
property is wired into the auth flow (fake-free).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

triage.rationale: Private-key SSH is already supported through PrivateKeyPath on PuTTY/OpenSSH; this patch depends on an absent SSH.NET protocol and incompatible properties.
